audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated locator (Novak et al. 2022 p.81 §6 Word Stress) in the PDF and text we hold. The deciding work is the 2022 English-language reference grammar that Glottolog ranks first for Karelian and that itself synthesizes 17 earlier grammars on exactly this point; StressTyp2/Hayes (via Leskinen 1984) independently agree. Coding 'fixed-strict' initial primary stress with odd-syllable non-final secondaries (stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 10100 (1 = a stressed syllable)) matches the source; the only wrinkles the sources mention (late Russian loans, optional ternary secondary shift, Ludic apocope keeping a final secondary) do not change the primary-stress class. No better stress-specific or instrumental study of Karelian was found in CrossRef

sources.quote: "Word stress in Karelian is constant. The primary stress always falls on the first syllable (pái-men / pái-moi 'a shepherd'), with the exception of some late Russian borrowings, in which the primary stress may sometimes fall on other syllables. In the standard varieties of Karelian stress can only be on the first syllable. tone.quote: Для карельского языка характерно фиксированное словесное ударение: главное ударение всегда падает на первый слог слова, второстепенное (более слабое) — на третий слог четырехсложного слова или на четвертый — пятисложного. В сложных словах главное ударение падает на первый слог слова, второстепенное — на первый слог второй части сложного слова.
tone.locator: section 'Структура языка > Фонетика' (end of section, immediately before 'Морфология'), web page, no pagination
tone.translation: Karelian is characterised by fixed word stress: primary stress always falls on the first syllable of the word, secondary (weaker) stress on the third syllable of a four-syllable word or the fourth of a five-syllable one. In compounds primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word, secondary stress on the first syllable of the second member. (End of the phonetics section; no tone/intonation statement.)

tone.quote: Ударение. Для карельского языка характерно фиксированное словесное ударение: главное ударение всегда падает на первый слог слова, второстепенное (более слабое) – на третий слог четырехсложного слова или на четвертый – пятисложного: háravóija ‘сгребать’, méččäníekkа ‘лесовик’, míelettö́myš ‘глупость’, páimendamíne ‘пастьба’, В сложных словах главное ударение падает на первый слог слова, второстепенное – на первый слог второй части сложного слова: kíelen|kándaja ‘сплетник’, pýhä|pä́ivä ‘воскресенье’, ýö|lákko ‘летучая мышь’, kúuži|méččä ‘ельник’.
tone.locator: p. 42 as printed, section 'Ударение' in the chapter Фонетика
tone.translation: Stress. Karelian is characterised by fixed word stress: primary stress always falls on the first syllable of the word, secondary (weaker) stress on the third syllable of a four-syllable word or the fourth of a five-syllable word [examples]. In compound words primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word and secondary stress on the first syllable of the second member of the compound [examples]. (This is the entire prosody section; tone/intonation are not mentioned.)
